name: Crownhall Checkers
subtitle: Four draughts rule sets
shortDescription: American, Russian, Brazilian and International draughts with a 3D board, Coach, Think hints and eight computer levels.
longDescription:
Draughts has been played for centuries, and every country that took it up wrote its own rules. Crownhall Checkers keeps four of them under one roof so you can feel the differences instead of reading about them.

American Checkers (English draughts) on 8x8 is the classic game. Russian Draughts (Shashki) adds flying kings, men that capture backward, and a man crowned mid-capture that keeps jumping. Brazilian Draughts plays the International rules on the small board with the majority-capture rule. International Draughts on 10x10 is the world championship game. Compulsory capture, flying kings and the draw rules are implemented exactly, and each Rules page explains them with diagrams.

Play against eight computer levels from Apprentice to Grandmaster, or Adaptive, which follows your results. Two players can share a device and the board turns toward whoever is to move. Auto Play lets the computer play both sides and explain what happens: tap Think for its plan or Take over to join. Take back moves, switch the Coach on to grade every move, or practise with puzzles.

The board is lit in real time with wooden pieces that stack when crowned. Text size goes up to 300 percent.

Crownhall Checkers is free with ads. Go ad-free with an optional monthly pass or by watching videos for ad-free time. Ads never appear during a capture sequence, and the game works offline with no account.
monetization: Free with ads, optional monthly ad-free
